subject.title: feat(exec): macOS sandbox-exec wrapper for host process isolation

question: Should macOS exec isolation be exposed as a model-call `sandboxProfile` parameter, or implemented as an operator-owned sandbox backend/profile under the existing sandbox contract?
rationale: This decides the execution security boundary, who controls permissive versus restrictive profiles, and whether a macOS-only host wrapper can coexist with the existing Docker/SSH/OpenShell sandbox model.

options.title: Use Existing Sandbox Contract
options.body: Route macOS support through backend/config policy and keep profile selection operator-owned, with no model-selected permissive profile unless explicitly approved.

options.title: Accept Per-Call Prototype
options.body: Allow the model-facing parameter as an experimental macOS-only surface, accepting the compatibility and security-boundary risk after live proof.

options.title: Replace The Branch
options.body: Close or pause this draft and ask for a new narrow PR after the sandbox roadmap decides the macOS boundary.

recommendation.title: Use Existing Sandbox Contract
recommendation.body: Route macOS support through backend/config policy and keep profile selection operator-owned, with no model-selected permissive profile unless explicitly approved.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the closest merged history on the exec sandbox security boundary changed by this PR.
